cases.application: The availability of a statutory appeal (s.127/Clause 6.8(d)) does not bar writ entertainment where natural justice is violated, the action is without jurisdiction, or fundamental rights are enforced — though on the facts here, the underlying technical/evidentiary controversy was left to be resolved through the departmental process rather than adjudicated directly by the writ court.

A.I. Champdany Industries Ltd. (municipa.name: A.I. Champdany Industries Ltd. (municipal dues case)
A.I. Champdany Industries Ltd. (municipa.proposition: Municipal dues, being unsecured and not within the purview of Crown debt, do not have priority/charge over a company's assets on liquidation sale.

cited_in.title: Palika Towns LLP v. State of U.P. & 2 Others
cited_in.how_treated: Distinguished — concerned unsecured municipal dues without a charge, unlike the lease deed's express first-charge clause here.

1396480.name: A.I.S.B. Officers Federation & Others v. Union of India & Others
1396480.proposition: A petitioner cannot raise mala fide allegations against persons who have not been impleaded as respondents.

cited_in.title: M/S Beeco Electrical India & Anr. v. Pashchimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Ors.
cited_in.how_treated: Relied on to the same effect.

1353689.name: A.R. Antulay v. R.S. Nayak and 38 further authorities on statutory interpretation, precedent (sub silentio/per incuriam), vires of delegated legislation, and harmonious construction (incl. Kunj Behari Lal Butail v. State of H.P.; Global Energy Ltd. v. CERC; State of T.N. v. P. Krishnamurthy; J.K. Cotton Spinning & Weaving Mills v. State of U.P.; PTC India v. CERC)
1353689.proposition: General canons of statutory interpretation and administrative law (reading a statute as a whole vs. section-by-section; ultra vires/consistency of subordinate legislation with the parent Act; precedential weight of a decision not engaging a specific provision) cited in support of the rival vires arguments.

cited_in.title: Kisan Cold Storage & Ice Factory v. Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Ors. (Full Bench reference)
cited_in.how_treated: Not individually discussed — the Court held the text of Section 42(5)-(7) and Rule 7 to be clear and unambiguous, so canvassing the case law would 'unnecessarily burden' the judgment.

1358956.name: Abdul Gani & Anr. v. State of U.P. & Ors.
1358956.citation: Civil Misc. Writ Petition No. 15498 of 2008
1358956.proposition: An assessment made only on the allegation of a tampered meter seal, without any evidence of how the seal was tampered or theft was effected, cannot stand.

cited_in.title: M/S Beeco Electrical India & Anr. v. Pashchimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Ors.
cited_in.how_treated: Distinguished on facts — unlike Abdul Gani, here there was affirmative evidence (naked conductor, MRI anomalies) of the manner of theft.

Abdus Salam @ A. Salam v. Election Commi.name: Abdus Salam @ A. Salam v. Election Commission of India
Abdus Salam @ A. Salam v. Election Commi.proposition: There is nothing rigid about natural justice; the duty to hear does not always mean affording a personal hearing.

cited_in.title: Hazi Mohd. Yaseen v. P.V.V.N.L. & Another
cited_in.how_treated: Referred (respondent's line).

28246.name: Ahmedabad Electricity Co. Ltd. v. Gujarat Inns Pvt. Ltd. & Ors.
28246.proposition: In the absence of any statutory provision, an auction-purchaser applying for a fresh connection cannot be fastened with the previous owner's electricity dues, and a fresh connection cannot be denied on that ground.

cited_in.title: Chandra Prakash Gupta v. State of U.P. & 3 Others
cited_in.how_treated: Distinguished — held inapplicable after Clause 4.1 of the 2005 Code supplied the statutory provision it presupposed to be absent.

cited_in.title: M/S Dharti Agro Industries Pvt. Ltd. v. The Managing Director, Pashchimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & 2 Others
cited_in.how_treated: Relied on by the petitioner as foundational auction-purchaser precedent.

1638274.name: Ajit Singh @ Muraha v. State of U.P. & Others
1638274.proposition: Reiterates the Bhajan Lal/Satya Pal standard that FIR quashing/stay of arrest is warranted only where no cognizable offence is ex-facie discernible or a statutory restriction on investigation exists.

cited_in.title: Pawan Kumar Laur v. State of U.P. & Others
cited_in.how_treated: Followed as the controlling Full Bench authority.

139734870.name: Aleque Padamsee & Others v. Union of India & Others
139734870.proposition: Where the police fail to act on information about a cognizable offence, the remedy is to file a complaint before the Magistrate under s.190/200 Cr.P.C., not a writ petition seeking a direction to register an FIR.

cited_in.title: Shiv Murti Yadav v. State of U.P. & 6 Others
cited_in.how_treated: Applied to hold the revisionist had no separate ground for interference given this remedy.

Aligarh Muslim University v. Mansoor Ali.name: Aligarh Muslim University v. Mansoor Ali Khan
Aligarh Muslim University v. Mansoor Ali.proposition: Following S.L. Kapoor v. Jagmohan, where on admitted/indisputable facts only one conclusion is possible, breach of natural justice need not vitiate the order (a narrow exception).

cited_in.title: Hazi Mohd. Yaseen v. P.V.V.N.L. & Another
cited_in.how_treated: Referred (respondent's line); the exception held inapplicable.

Allahabad Inter Prises v. State of U.P..name: Allahabad Inter Prises v. State of U.P.
Allahabad Inter Prises v. State of U.P..proposition: A 'Protective Load' charge cannot be raised in the absence of any option exercised by the consumer for that facility.

cited_in.title: Executive Engineer, Electricity Urban Distribution Division v. The Electricity Ombudsman & 2 Others
cited_in.how_treated: Followed to hold the protective-load demand unsustainable.

163340936.name: Anand Kumar v. State of U.P.
163340936.proposition: A tenant, being an 'occupier' under Clause 2(oo), has a statutory right to apply for and obtain a connection on fulfilling the Code's conditions (mainly an indemnity bond). [SCJ-006 in this corpus.]

cited_in.title: Dr. Ashok Kumar Sharma & Another v. State of U.P. & 4 Others
cited_in.how_treated: Distinguished — ratio held not squarely applicable, since it presupposes authorised occupation, absent here given the unstayed eviction decree.

Andhra Steel Corporation Ltd. v. A.P. St.name: Andhra Steel Corporation Ltd. v. A.P. State Electricity Board

cited_in.title: Jharkhand State Electricity Board & Others v. M/s Ramkrishna Forging Limited
cited_in.how_treated: Distinguished on facts as relating to minimum-guarantee charge under the old 1910 Act.

897981.name: Ashok Kumar & Others v. State of U.P.
897981.proposition: Where the challenge to a Section 126 assessment involves purely legal/jurisdictional issues (including the vires of a notification), which the assessing officer or the s.127 appellate authority cannot decide, the writ petition is entertained without relegating the party to the alternative remedy.

cited_in.title: Kapil Gupta v. U.P. Power Corpn. Ltd. & Anr.
cited_in.how_treated: Distinguished — inapplicable to a pure factual challenge with no vires/jurisdictional issue.

cited_in.title: Latif v. State of U.P. & Ors.
cited_in.how_treated: Followed and applied in full — the impugned bill-cum-notice and demand notice were set aside for non-compliance with the Clause 6.8 procedure as laid down in Ashok Kumar.

cited_in.title: M/S Beeco Electrical India & Anr. v. Pashchimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Ors.
cited_in.how_treated: Distinguished on facts — the requirement was held satisfied since the checking report itself disclosed the manner (naked conductor at LT mains bracket); the consumer's failure to explain it defeated his reliance on Ashok Kumar.

cited_in.title: M/S Kissan Chilling Udyog & Anr. v. State of U.P. & Ors.
cited_in.how_treated: Followed and applied; the impugned orders were quashed for non-compliance and misreading of the underlying checking report.

cited_in.title: M/S Modern Rice Mill v. MVVNL & Anr.
cited_in.how_treated: Followed and extensively relied on for both the Clause 6.8 procedure and the Secure Meter technical background.

cited_in.title: M/S Om Ice Factory Thru' Its Partner Satyapal Singh v. Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Anr.
cited_in.how_treated: Distinguished — no jurisdictional/vires issue was raised here, only a factual challenge to the assessment already considered by the authority.

cited_in.title: M/S Trikoot Iron & Steels Castings Ltd. v. State of U.P. & Ors.
cited_in.how_treated: Followed.

cited_in.title: M/S Urmila Oil Industries v. U.P. Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam & Ors.
cited_in.how_treated: Followed and applied to quash an assessment resting on mere 'possibility' of theft without Clause 6.8 compliance.

cited_in.title: M/S Venus Stone Crushing Co. & Anr. v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd. & Ors.
cited_in.how_treated: Followed; the assessment procedure was found not to have been complied with in this case either.

cited_in.title: Sandeep Kesarwani v. State of U.P. & 3 Others
cited_in.how_treated: Followed for the genus/species relationship between ss.126 and 135 and the natural-justice requirement.

cited_in.title: Sanjay Rizvi v. M.D. Kanpur Electricity Supply Co. & Others
cited_in.how_treated: Relied on by the licensee to justify its compliance with directions in that case; also relied on by the petitioner to support writ maintainability.

cited_in.title: Shishir Jain v. Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Another
cited_in.how_treated: Followed as supporting authority for the natural-justice requirement.

cited_in.title: Shri Kunwar Sarvesh Kumar Singh v. Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Ors.
cited_in.how_treated: Cited (via the pari materia Clause 6.8 analogy) for the content-sufficiency requirement of a show-cause notice.

Awadesh S. Pandey v. Tata Power Corporat.name: Awadesh S. Pandey v. Tata Power Corporation Ltd.
Awadesh S. Pandey v. Tata Power Corporat.proposition: Section 56(2)'s two-year bar limits only the special coercive remedy of disconnection under s.56(1); it does not extinguish the underlying debt or bar recovery of a sum falling within two years of the demand, and does not preclude independent recovery by suit.

cited_in.title: Shyam Ferrous Ltd. Gopal Nagar v. State of U.P. & 6 Others
cited_in.how_treated: Cited as persuasive authority on the limited scope of s.56(2), though the Court found the broader question of Paliwal Alloys' correctness academic on the facts and left it open.

35346928.name: Balram Prasad v. Kunal Saha & Ors.
35346928.proposition: The court is sceptical of a strait-jacket multiplier method and may deviate from it to avoid over- or under-compensation, determining just, fair and reasonable compensation on the facts.

cited_in.title: Executive Engineer, Electricity Distribution Division-II v. State of U.P. & 2 Others
cited_in.how_treated: Relied on (¶124 quoted) for a flexible, just-compensation approach.

56328920.name: Bar Council of India v. Union of India
56328920.proposition: Permanent Lok Adalats under Chapter VI-A of the LSA Act, 1987 have jurisdiction over disputes concerning public utility services (including supply of power) up to a pecuniary limit, in addition to and not in derogation of other fora, before the dispute is brought to a court.

cited_in.title: Divisional Engineer, Electricity Distribution Division-I v. Raman Singh & Another
cited_in.how_treated: Relied on to sustain the Permanent Lok Adalat's jurisdiction.

cited_in.title: Executive Engineer, Electricity Distribution Division-II v. State of U.P. & 2 Others
cited_in.how_treated: Relied on to sustain the Permanent Lok Adalat's jurisdiction and its validity.

477052.name: Benarsi Silk Palace v. Commr. of Income Tax
477052.proposition: Jurisdiction can be conferred only by statute, not by consent or acquiescence — an assessee cannot confer jurisdiction on the Income Tax Officer by waiving a statutory notice requirement.

cited_in.title: M.D., Pakshimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. v. Electricity Ombudsman & Anr.
cited_in.how_treated: Relied on for the no-jurisdiction-by-consent principle in a taxation analogy.

1022604.name: Bharat Barrel & Drum Manufacturing Co. Pvt. Ltd. v. Municipal Corporation of Greater Bombay
1022604.proposition: There is no limitation for making a demand by way of supplementary bill; constructive res judicata does not apply to bar a supplementary demand for previously unclaimed misuse charges.

cited_in.title: Shyam Ferrous Ltd. Gopal Nagar v. State of U.P. & 6 Others
cited_in.how_treated: Approved and applied (as endorsed by Swastic Industries).

1384523.name: Bharathidasan University & Anr. v. All-India Council for Technical Education & Ors.
1384523.proposition: (Same proposition as Chandra Kumar Shah — regulation-making power is not a source of independent legislative authority.)

cited_in.title: M/S Dev Prayag Paper Mill (Pvt.) & Ors. v. State of U.P. & Ors. (batch of ~90 connected writ petitions)
cited_in.how_treated: Cited to the same effect; not examined in detail for the same reason.

Bihar State Electricity Board v. M/s Gre.name: Bihar State Electricity Board v. M/s Green Rubber Industries
Bihar State Electricity Board v. M/s Gre.proposition: On minimum-guarantee charge (under the Electricity Act, 1910).

cited_in.title: Jharkhand State Electricity Board & Others v. M/s Ramkrishna Forging Limited
cited_in.how_treated: Distinguished on facts as relating to minimum-guarantee charge under the old 1910 Act.

Bihar State Electricity Board v. Parmesh.name: Bihar State Electricity Board v. Parmeshwar Kumar Agarwala
Bihar State Electricity Board v. Parmesh.proposition: The Supply Code / conditions of supply have statutory flavour and are to be strictly followed by the parties.

cited_in.title: Hazi Mohd. Yaseen v. P.V.V.N.L. & Another
cited_in.how_treated: Referred for the statutory character of the Supply Code.

1336883.name: Bimal Kumar Gupta v. Special Police Establishment Lokayukt
1336883.proposition: Employees of the Madhya Pradesh State Electricity Board are not 'public servants' for purposes of prosecution under the Prevention of Corruption Act, since s.81 of the 1948 Act only deems them public servants under IPC s.21, and a 'deemed provision' cannot extend to another statute (relying on State of Maharashtra v. Laljit Rajashi Shah).

cited_in.title: Naresh Kumar Madan v. State of Madhya Pradesh
cited_in.how_treated: Overruled — held not to lay down the correct law; the 1988 Act's own broader 'public servant' definition (s.2(1)(c)(iii)) independently captures Board employees regardless of the 1948 Act's IPC-specific deeming fiction.

1350255.name: Binani Zinc Ltd. v. Kerala State Electricity Board & Ors.
1350255.proposition: The regulatory commission has not been empowered to frame tariff with retrospective effect covering a period before its own constitution/determination; the rule of law postulates that all laws are prospective, absent an express provision or necessary intendment to the contrary.

cited_in.title: M/S Shokumbhari Pulp & Paper Mills Ltd. v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd. & 3 Others (with connected petitions)
cited_in.how_treated: Followed and applied to quash the retrospective tariff notification.

569235.name: Board of Trustees, Port of Mumbai v. Indian Oil Corporation
569235.proposition: Port dues under the Major Port Trust Act, 1963 override all other claims, including secured creditors, in liquidation.

cited_in.title: Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. v. Raman Ispat Private Limited & Ors.
cited_in.how_treated: Held inapplicable/distinguishable in light of the IBC's later, comprehensive waterfall mechanism under s.53.

316379.name: Bombay Electric Supply and Transport Undertaking v. Laffans (India) Pvt. Ltd. & Anr.
316379.proposition: Under the Indian Electricity Act, 1910, the Electrical Inspector is the appropriate person to adjudicate a dispute regarding meter accuracy underlying a bill, functioning as a form of independent statutory arbitration.

cited_in.title: Mohamdabad Cold Storage Private Ltd. (& Anr.) v. Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Ors.
cited_in.how_treated: Applied by analogy to hold that s.162 of the Electricity Act, 2003 (Chief Electrical Inspector/Electrical Inspector) is the modern successor forum for such meter-accuracy disputes.

cited_in.title: Mother India Refrigeration Industries (& Anr.) v. Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Ors.
cited_in.how_treated: Applied by analogy to hold that s.162 of the Electricity Act, 2003 is the modern successor forum for such meter-accuracy disputes (companion citation to SCJ-083).

Broom's Legal Maxims (10th Edn.), p. 191.name: Broom's Legal Maxims (10th Edn.), p. 191
Broom's Legal Maxims (10th Edn.), p. 191.proposition: No man shall take advantage of his own wrong — recognised in courts of law and of equity.

cited_in.title: Indian Oil Corporation Ltd. v. State of U.P. & 3 Others
cited_in.how_treated: Extracted (¶ 56) in support of the maxim.

197296101.name: BSES Ltd. v. Tata Power Co. Ltd.
197296101.proposition: An interim arrangement, based on a prima facie view without full examination, would be subject to final adjustment with interest where a matter (there, standby charges) was pending Commission determination and remained unpaid.

cited_in.title: M/S NTPC Ltd. v. M.P. State Electricity Board & Ors. (with connected appeals)
cited_in.how_treated: Distinguished — that case involved a dispute referred for determination and unpaid pending resolution, unlike the present case where the interim tariff was lawfully charged and paid per standing notifications.

Carborundum Universal Ltd. v. CBDT.name: Carborundum Universal Ltd. v. CBDT
Carborundum Universal Ltd. v. CBDT.proposition: Where a statutory provision does not exclude natural justice, an opportunity of being heard is to be assumed, especially in quasi-judicial proceedings.

cited_in.title: Hazi Mohd. Yaseen v. P.V.V.N.L. & Another
cited_in.how_treated: Referred in the natural-justice discussion.

33926990.name: Central GST Delhi-III v. Delhi International Airport Ltd.
33926990.proposition: User Development Fee (UDF) is in the nature of a tax or cess collected to fund future projects, not consideration for a service, and is therefore not exigible to service tax.

cited_in.title: Suman Engineering and Chemicals Pvt. Ltd. v. U.P.P.C.L. & 4 Others
cited_in.how_treated: Cited by the respondents to characterise system-loading charges as a non-refundable exaction; distinguished — that case concerned only the leviability of service tax on UDF, collected from persons actually liable, and “is of no help to the respondents.”

15924357.name: Chairman, SBI v. M.J. James
15924357.proposition: The court must consciously examine whether a party has sat over a matter and woken up to gain advantage; delay and laches are balanced accordingly.

cited_in.title: Indian Oil Corporation Ltd. v. State of U.P. & 3 Others
cited_in.how_treated: Quoted (¶ 55); relied on to weigh the licensee's sitting-over against its demand.

759180.name: Chairman, West Bengal State Electricity Board & Ors. v. Syed Mukbul Hossain & Ors.
759180.proposition: In the matter of theft of electrical energy, the assessment is referable to Section 126 and appeal is to be filed under Section 127.

cited_in.title: M/S Trikoot Iron & Steels Castings Ltd. v. State of U.P. & Ors.
cited_in.how_treated: Followed as the leading authority for the s.126/s.127 characterisation of theft assessments.

cited_in.title: Sandeep Kesarwani v. State of U.P. & 3 Others
cited_in.how_treated: Cited for the general availability of s.127 appeal in theft-adjacent assessment cases.

895706.name: Chandavarkar Sita Ratna Rao v. Ashalata S. Guram
895706.proposition: A non obstante clause gives the enacting part overriding effect over the provisions mentioned in it.

93465500.name: Jindal Poly Films Limited v. U.P. Electricity Regulatory Commission, Lucknow
93465500.proposition: Regulation 8.1(i) of the 2007 Regulations, giving the Distribution Licensee a remedy of representation to the Electricity Ombudsman, is intra vires the Act, 2003, on a 'read as a whole' construction.

cited_in.title: Kisan Cold Storage & Ice Factory v. Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Ors. (Full Bench reference)
cited_in.how_treated: Overruled — did not engage Section 42(5)-(7) specifically; does not lay down the correct law.

73508068.name: K. Kishan v. Vijay Nirman Company Private Limited
73508068.proposition: Upholds the primacy of IBC s.238 over the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996.

cited_in.title: M/S Dharti Agro Industries Pvt. Ltd. v. The Managing Director, Pashchimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & 2 Others
cited_in.how_treated: Referred as another instance of IBC primacy.

28868630.name: K. Shashidhar v. Indian Overseas Bank
28868630.proposition: Once the conditions of s.33 IBC are met, the Adjudicating Authority must initiate liquidation as a matter of course, with no discretion to evaluate the CoC's commercial decision.

cited_in.title: Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. v. Raman Ispat Private Limited & Ors.
cited_in.how_treated: Cited for the mandatory, non-discretionary nature of liquidation initiation under s.33.

160269658.name: K.C. Ninan v. Kerala State Electricity Board
160269658.proposition: Electricity utilities can, by subordinate legislation or statutory conditions of supply, create a charge enabling recovery of electricity arrears from a subsequent transferee; recoupment of arrears protects the public good of electricity supply.

cited_in.title: Amir Ahmad v. State of U.P. & 4 Others
cited_in.how_treated: Followed and applied to hold the auction-purchaser liable to clear arrears before a new connection is released.

cited_in.title: M/S Dharti Agro Industries Pvt. Ltd. v. The Managing Director, Pashchimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & 2 Others
cited_in.cited_by: Petitioner and Respondent (both relied on it, for opposite conclusions)
cited_in.how_treated: Distinguished/confined — held applicable only outside the IBC framework; does not govern where the utility has itself participated in and lodged a claim in an IBC liquidation.

cited_in.title: M/S Santosh Preservation Pvt. Ltd. & Anr. v. Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Anr.
cited_in.how_treated: Referred to support a purposive interpretation of Clause 5.6 that does not create an artificial independent-testing right in cases of patent, visible meter tampering.

K.V. Rajalakshmiah Setty v. State of Mys.name: K.V. Rajalakshmiah Setty v. State of Mysore
K.V. Rajalakshmiah Setty v. State of Mys.proposition: A mere representation is not an adequate explanation for delay in approaching the court.

cited_in.title: M/S Three Star Paper Mills Pvt. Ltd. v. State of U.P. & 5 Ors.
cited_in.how_treated: Relied on.

Kali Das Wadhwani & Anr. v. Jagjiwan Das.name: Kali Das Wadhwani & Anr. v. Jagjiwan Das & Anr.
Kali Das Wadhwani & Anr. v. Jagjiwan Das.proposition: Jurisdiction cannot be conferred by consent, acquiescence or waiver where there is none; these factors are relevant only to pecuniary/territorial jurisdiction, not inherent jurisdiction, the absence of which renders a decree a nullity.

cited_in.title: M.D., Pakshimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. v. Electricity Ombudsman & Anr.
cited_in.how_treated: Relied on.

Kamil v. State of U.P. & Others.name: Kamil v. State of U.P. & Others
Kamil v. State of U.P. & Others.proposition: Same procedural-fairness principle for s.126/Clause 8.1 assessment.

cited_in.title: Shishir Jain v. Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Another
cited_in.how_treated: Followed as supporting authority.

Karnal Improvement Trust v. Prakashwanti.name: Karnal Improvement Trust v. Prakashwanti
Karnal Improvement Trust v. Prakashwanti.proposition: Acquiescence does not confer jurisdiction, and an erroneous interpretation should not be perpetuated defeating legislative intent.

cited_in.title: M.D., Pakshimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. v. Electricity Ombudsman & Anr.
cited_in.how_treated: Relied on.

708348.name: Kavita Trehan & Anr. v. Balsara Hygiene Products Ltd.
708348.proposition: The power to make restitution is inherent in every court, applying even outside Section 144 CPC.

cited_in.title: M/S NTPC Ltd. v. M.P. State Electricity Board & Ors. (with connected appeals)
cited_in.how_treated: Distinguished — that case involved wrongful termination of a contract and an injunction in a civil suit, factually inapposite here; the Tribunal itself found no coercive extraction by NTPC.

Khem Chand v. Union of India.name: Khem Chand v. Union of India
Khem Chand v. Union of India.proposition: A 'reasonable opportunity' of showing cause includes an opportunity of a personal hearing (in the service-inquiry context).

cited_in.title: Hazi Mohd. Yaseen v. P.V.V.N.L. & Another
cited_in.how_treated: Discussed and distinguished as a service matter, but its principle supported requiring a personal hearing here.

546415.name: Khem Chand v. Union of India & Ors.
546415.proposition: Lays down the content and standard of 'reasonable opportunity' of hearing to be afforded before an adverse order.

cited_in.title: Lalit Kumar Kapoor v. Kanpur Electricity Supply Company & Anr.
cited_in.how_treated: Relied on to define the standard of reasonable opportunity applicable before a theft-based Section 126 assessment.

1625415.name: Kiran Singh v. Chaman Paswan
1625415.proposition: A defect of jurisdiction strikes at the very authority of the Court to pass any decree and cannot be cured even by consent of parties.

cited_in.title: M.D., Pakshimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. v. Electricity Ombudsman & Anr.
cited_in.how_treated: Relied on to the same effect.

Kirpa Singh v. Ajaypal Singh.name: Kirpa Singh v. Ajaypal Singh
Kirpa Singh v. Ajaypal Singh.proposition: Right of appeal governed by law at the date of institution of the suit, not at the date of decision or of filing the appeal.

cited_in.title: Aruna Bhargava v. PuVVNL & Another
cited_in.how_treated: Referred; approved in Garikapati.

22637242.name: Kunwar Sarvesh Kumar Singh v. Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Ors.
22637242.proposition: In theft cases, the Clause 8.1 assessment procedure of the Supply Code, 2005 applies.

cited_in.title: Sandeep Kesarwani v. State of U.P. & 3 Others
cited_in.how_treated: Followed as consistent authority for the Clause 8.1 procedure applying to theft assessments.

655432.name: Kusheshwar Prasad Singh v. State of Bihar
655432.proposition: An authority cannot take undue advantage of its own default in discharging a statutory duty; a wrongdoer ought not to profit from his own wrong.

cited_in.title: Indian Oil Corporation Ltd. v. State of U.P. & 3 Others
cited_in.how_treated: Quoted (¶ 54) and applied to the licensee's 7-year delay in disconnecting and 10-year delay in amending.

1873931.name: Kusumam Hotels (P) Ltd. v. Kerala State Electricity Board & Others
1873931.proposition: Section 56(2) of the Electricity Act, 2003 applies only after the Act came into force; the bar of limitation does not apply to liabilities of a consumer incurred prior to the Act's commencement, given s.6 of the General Clauses Act preserving accrued liabilities on repeal.

cited_in.title: Shyam Ferrous Ltd. Gopal Nagar v. State of U.P. & 6 Others
cited_in.how_treated: Applied as the controlling authority to hold s.56(2) inapplicable to the pre-2003-Act peak-hour penalty liability.

33418694.name: Lalit Kumar Jain v. Union of India & Ors.
33418694.proposition: Approval of a resolution plan under s.31 IBC does not ipso facto discharge a personal guarantor of a Corporate Debtor of liability under the contract of guarantee; release of the principal borrower by an involuntary process (insolvency/liquidation) does not absolve the guarantor, whose liability arises from an independent contract.

cited_in.title: Narendra Singh Panwar v. Pashchimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & 2 Others
cited_in.how_treated: Applied as the leading authority for rejecting the discharge argument; extent of liability held to depend on the guarantee's own terms.

12052125.name: Laxmi Pat Surana v. Union of India & Anr.
12052125.proposition: IBC is a complete, beneficiary code intended to rehabilitate the Corporate Debtor, not merely a money-recovery statute; a Corporate Debtor's guarantor liability is coextensive and coterminous with the principal borrower's obligation under s.128 of the Contract Act.

cited_in.title: Narendra Singh Panwar v. Pashchimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & 2 Others
cited_in.how_treated: Cited for the general character of the IBC and the coextensive nature of guarantor liability.

LML Ltd., Kanpur v. State of U.P..name: LML Ltd., Kanpur v. State of U.P.
LML Ltd., Kanpur v. State of U.P..proposition: A tariff approved by the Regulatory Commission alone can be implemented by a licensee, which has no power to alter or vary it; a licensee circular inconsistent with the approved tariff is void and inoperative.

cited_in.title: Northern Coalfield Ltd. v. Chairman and Managing Director, U.P. Power Corporation Ltd. & Ors.
cited_in.how_treated: Followed on the general principle (undisputed by both parties); its specific observations on restricted-hours surcharge were treated as obiter and not relied on, since that case did not involve a consumer who had in fact used power during restricted hours.

1274811.name: M. Rathinaswami & Ors. v. State of Tamil Nadu & Ors.
1274811.proposition: To save a statutory provision from unconstitutionality, a restricted or extended interpretation may sometimes be required.

cited_in.title: Northern Coalfield Ltd. v. Chairman and Managing Director, U.P. Power Corporation Ltd. & Ors.
cited_in.how_treated: Held inapplicable — the non obstante clause in Rule 8(3)-equivalent tariff language here was clear and unambiguous, raising no constitutionality concern requiring a saving interpretation.

1848972.name: M.K. Shah Engineers & Contractors v. State of M.P.
1848972.proposition: No one may take advantage of one's own wrong; a party whose conduct disables a preceding procedural step is deemed to have waived it.

cited_in.title: Indian Oil Corporation Ltd. v. State of U.P. & 3 Others
cited_in.how_treated: Quoted (¶ 51) and applied: the prerequisite of amending the agreement deemed waived within a reasonable time of the consumer's request.

1082759.name: M/s Isha Marbles v. Bihar State Electricity Board
1082759.proposition: Section 24 of the Indian Electricity Act, 1910 confers a statutory right on the Board to cut off supply for non-payment, without prejudice to (and not limited by) its separate right to sue.

cited_in.title: Shyam Ferrous Ltd. Gopal Nagar v. State of U.P. & 6 Others
cited_in.how_treated: Applied to hold s.24's demand/recovery power is not time-barred merely because a suit-based recovery might be subject to civil limitation.

1595240.name: M/s JMD Alloys Limited v. Bihar State Electricity Board
1595240.proposition: Sending a disputed Secure Meter for testing to its manufacturer's own accredited laboratory is likely to create a strong bias in favour of the supplier/manufacturer, even if the laboratory is accredited.

cited_in.title: M/S Modern Rice Mill v. MVVNL & Anr.
cited_in.how_treated: Followed to hold that the manufacturer's testing report cannot be relied upon as an 'independent laboratory' report.

M/s Kesarwani Sheetalaya & Others v. Pur.name: M/s Kesarwani Sheetalaya & Others v. Purvanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Others
M/s Kesarwani Sheetalaya & Others v. Pur.citation: Civil Misc. Writ Petition No. 2309 of 2009, decided 9.10.2009
M/s Kesarwani Sheetalaya & Others v. Pur.proposition: Where a tapping consumer had itself obtained the original consumer's consent and shared the feeder's construction cost, it stands at par with the original consumer, and a further connection through tapping to another consumer without ITS consent violates Clause 3.4(d)(ii).

cited_in.title: M/S Shri Parasnath Alloys (Pvt.) Ltd. v. Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Ors.
cited_in.how_treated: Distinguished — the petitioner here had not obtained the true original consumer's consent or shared the feeder's own construction cost, unlike the petitioners in Kesarwani Sheetalaya.

158917471.name: M/S Lipton India Ltd. & Others v. Union of India & Others
158917471.proposition: Though no limitation period is prescribed for Article 226 petitions, they should ordinarily be filed within a reasonable time.

cited_in.title: M/S Three Star Paper Mills Pvt. Ltd. v. State of U.P. & 5 Ors.
cited_in.how_treated: Relied on.

1883604.name: M/s Modern Rice Mill v. Madhyanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Another
1883604.proposition: Clause 5.6(d) mandates a specific procedure before meter testing — information to the consumer of the proposed testing date, an opportunity to be present (personally or through a representative), obtaining signature if present, and a right to dispute the testing under Clause 5.6(c).

cited_in.title: Saurabh Agrawal & Another v. State of U.P. & Others
cited_in.how_treated: Applied to hold the meter-testing procedure was not followed, undermining the theft allegation.

M/s Modern Rice Mill v. MVVNL & Anr..name: M/s Modern Rice Mill v. MVVNL & Anr.
M/s Modern Rice Mill v. MVVNL & Anr..proposition: A meter manufacturer's own lab cannot be an 'independent laboratory'; testing by the manufacturer amounts to making a person judge in his own cause, given its commercial interest in defending its product's tamper-proof reputation.

cited_in.title: M/S Venus Stone Crushing Co. & Anr. v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd. & Ors.
cited_in.how_treated: Followed and quoted at length.

57045694.name: M/s Mohit Paper Mills Ltd. & Anr. v. PVVNL & Ors.
57045694.proposition: Mens rea is not a requirement for a Section 126 civil assessment, as distinct from a Section 135 criminal prosecution.

cited_in.title: M/S Beeco Electrical India & Anr. v. Pashchimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Ors.
cited_in.how_treated: Agreed with and followed on the s.126/s.135 mens rea distinction.

cited_in.title: M/S Modern Rice Mill v. MVVNL & Anr.
cited_in.how_treated: Relied on (a companion judgment by the same Judge, five days earlier) for the technical background of the Secure Meter.

cited_in.title: M/S Trikoot Iron & Steels Castings Ltd. v. State of U.P. & Ors.
cited_in.how_treated: Followed/referred.

cited_in.title: Shri Kunwar Sarvesh Kumar Singh v. Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Ors.
cited_in.how_treated: Followed as the controlling precedent on which Supply Code procedure governs theft assessment.

1777029.name: M/s Paliwal Alloys (Pvt.) Ltd. v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd. & Others
1777029.proposition: Assessment under Section 126 is also to be made in theft cases, and the consumer has a right of appeal.

cited_in.title: M/S Trikoot Iron & Steels Castings Ltd. v. State of U.P. & Ors.
cited_in.how_treated: Followed.

cited_in.title: Sandeep Kesarwani v. State of U.P. & 3 Others
cited_in.how_treated: Distinguished from the petitioner's reading — clarified that the 'different fields' holding does not mean s.126 assessment is barred wherever s.135 also applies; rather, both provisions can and do operate concurrently on overlapping conduct.

cited_in.title: Sandeep Kesarwani v. State of U.P. & 3 Others
cited_in.how_treated: Followed as the controlling Division Bench precedent (with one member common to the present Bench).

cited_in.title: Sandeep Kesarwani v. State of U.P. & 3 Others
cited_in.how_treated: Followed for the overlapping-but-parallel operation of ss.126 and 135.

cited_in.title: Shyam Ferrous Ltd. Gopal Nagar v. State of U.P. & 6 Others
cited_in.how_treated: Distinguished as having been decided without the benefit of the later Kusumam Hotels ruling (16.5.2008), which was not brought to that Division Bench's attention; its correctness on the broader s.56(2) scope question left open for a future case.

M/s Popcorn Entertainment v. City Indust.name: M/s Popcorn Entertainment v. City Industrial Development Corporation
M/s Popcorn Entertainment v. City Indust.proposition: A writ may be entertained despite an alternative remedy where the action is without jurisdiction, or in breach of natural justice, or violates fundamental rights.

cited_in.title: Kapil Gupta v. U.P. Power Corpn. Ltd. & Anr.
cited_in.how_treated: Referred (through Ashok Kumar) for the three exceptions, held inapplicable here.

477172.name: M/s Shiv Flour and Rice Mills v. State of U.P. & Others
477172.citation: Civil Misc. Writ Petition No. 32927 of 2003
477172.proposition: Distinguishes 'service line' (Para 2.2(bb)) from 'independent feeder' (Para 2.2(ff)); without fulfilling Clause 3.4(d)'s conditions, the licensee cannot allow tapping of an independent feeder to supply another consumer running an arc/induction furnace, rolling mill or steel plant.

cited_in.title: M/S Shri Parasnath Alloys (Pvt.) Ltd. v. Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Ors.
cited_in.how_treated: Cited alongside Kesarwani Sheetalaya for the general Clause 3.4/consent framework; the petitioner's reliance nonetheless failed on the 'original consumer' facts.

764540.name: M/s Swastic Industries v. Maharashtra State Electricity Board
764540.proposition: There is no limitation for making a demand by way of supplementary bill under s.24 of the 1910 Act; the right to file suit is a separate option, not a precondition; the word 'due' should be given a wide, commercially-honest meaning.

cited_in.title: Shyam Ferrous Ltd. Gopal Nagar v. State of U.P. & 6 Others
cited_in.how_treated: Followed as directly on point for the 'no limitation on demand' proposition and the interpretation of 'due'.

M/s Uttarakhand Power Corporation Ltd. v.name: M/s Uttarakhand Power Corporation Ltd. v. M/s Shyam Baba Developers & Builders Pvt. Ltd.
M/s Uttarakhand Power Corporation Ltd. v.proposition: K.C. Ninan is not applicable where the electricity authority has filed a claim in liquidation proceedings.

cited_in.title: M/S Dharti Agro Industries Pvt. Ltd. v. The Managing Director, Pashchimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & 2 Others
cited_in.how_treated: Relied on by the petitioner and accepted by the Court to confine K.C. Ninan outside the IBC context.

508231.name: Madhya Pradesh Electricity Board v. Union of India & Ors.
508231.proposition: The Electricity (Supply) Act, 1948 provides for the constitution and composition of State Electricity Boards, each State being enjoined to constitute one.

cited_in.title: Naresh Kumar Madan v. State of Madhya Pradesh
cited_in.how_treated: Cited for the general statutory background on the constitution of Electricity Boards.

608550.name: Madhya Pradesh State Cooperative Dairy Federation Ltd. v. Rajnesh Kumar Jamindar
608550.proposition: (Cited among the mala fide-doctrine authorities; held inapplicable on facts.)

cited_in.title: M/S Beeco Electrical India & Anr. v. Pashchimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Ors.
cited_in.how_treated: Held not applicable to the facts of the case.

364995.name: Mahabir Kishore v. State of M.P.
364995.proposition: Under s.17(1)(c) of the Limitation Act, 1963, in a case of relief on the ground of mistake, limitation does not begin until the plaintiff has discovered, or could with reasonable diligence have discovered, the mistake.

cited_in.title: Assistant Engineer (D1), Ajmer Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Anr. v. Rahamatullah Khan alias Rahamjulla
cited_in.how_treated: Relied on to fix the limitation start-point at discovery of the billing mistake.

254621.name: Mahanta Moti Das v. S.P. Sahid
254621.proposition: Where a question involves investigation of complicated facts and recording of evidence, the High Court may refuse to decide it in a writ proceeding.

cited_in.title: Kapil Gupta v. U.P. Power Corpn. Ltd. & Anr.
cited_in.how_treated: Referred (within New Okhla) on declining writ jurisdiction over complex facts.

Managing Director (MIG), Hindustan Aeron.name: Managing Director (MIG), Hindustan Aeronautics Ltd. v. Ajit Prasad Tarway
Managing Director (MIG), Hindustan Aeron.proposition: The High Court's supervisory jurisdiction under Article 227 is not to be exercised to interfere with concurrent findings/orders of the courts below as if in appeal.

cited_in.title: Dipali Dey (Baxi) v. Mira Das
cited_in.how_treated: Referred in support of non-interference under Article 227.

57894.name: Manujendra Dutt v. Purnedu Prosad Roy Chowdhury
57894.proposition: Deletion of a provision (there, s.29 of the Calcutta Thika Tenancy Act) does not divest the forum of jurisdiction over proceedings validly transferred and pending before it, absent a contrary provision.

cited_in.title: Aruna Bhargava v. PuVVNL & Another
cited_in.how_treated: Relied on.

634758.name: Maria Cristina De Souza Sodder v. Amria Zurana Pereira Pinto
634758.proposition: The right of appeal is a substantive right that vests when the lis commences and is not affected by a repeal unless the repealing enactment expressly or by necessary implication takes it away.

cited_in.title: Aruna Bhargava v. PuVVNL & Another
cited_in.how_treated: Relied on.

779489.name: MCD v. H.D. Shourie
779489.proposition: Electricity charges become due, and limitation for their recovery commences, only when the bill is raised — not from the date of underlying consumption/default.

cited_in.title: Shyam Ferrous Ltd. Gopal Nagar v. State of U.P. & 6 Others
cited_in.how_treated: Followed to hold the 2002 violations only 'became due' upon the 2009 bill.

1553487.name: Member, Board of Revenue v. Anthony Paul Benthall
1553487.proposition: When a statute uses two different expressions in consecutive provisions, they cannot be construed as having the same meaning.

cited_in.title: Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. v. Raman Ispat Private Limited & Ors.
cited_in.how_treated: Applied to hold 'secured creditor' dues and 'government dues' are distinct categories under s.53 IBC, not interchangeable.

1921960.name: Modern Syntax (I) Ltd. v. Debts Recovery Tribunal, Jaipur
1921960.proposition: The provisions of a Relief Undertaking Act, being meant to sub-serve public interest and prevent unemployment, are to be given a liberal interpretation.

cited_in.title: Kanpur Electricity Supply Co. Ltd. & Anr. v. M/s L.M.L. Limited & Ors.
cited_in.how_treated: Relied on (by the respondent) for a liberal, revival-oriented reading of the relief regime.

1795995.name: Mohd. Sagir v. Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
1795995.proposition: A tampered meter is also a 'defective meter' within Clause 5.6 (read with Clause 5.9(a)(ii)); where tampering (a foreign remote-sensing device) was not visible on inspection and was established only by a subsequent committee's opening of the meter, the consumer had a right under Clause 5.6(c)(iii) to independent testing.

cited_in.title: M/S Santosh Preservation Pvt. Ltd. & Anr. v. Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Anr.
cited_in.how_treated: Distinguished — that case involved tampering not obvious at inspection, established only by later test/committee report, unlike the patent tampering here.

Mrutunjay Pani v. Narmada Bala Sasmal.name: Mrutunjay Pani v. Narmada Bala Sasmal
Mrutunjay Pani v. Narmada Bala Sasmal.proposition: Commodum ex injuria sua nemo habere debet — no one can be allowed to benefit from his own wrongful act.

cited_in.title: Indian Oil Corporation Ltd. v. State of U.P. & 3 Others
cited_in.how_treated: Quoted (¶ 53) as the foundation of the maxim; applied against the licensee's default.

72255341.name: MSEDCL v. JSW Steel Ltd.
72255341.proposition: Captive consumers bear no additional surcharge under s.42(4) even when not drawing from the licensee; such a levy would be discriminatory.

cited_in.title: Indian Oil Corporation Ltd. v. State of U.P. & 3 Others
cited_in.how_treated: Cited by the petitioner (¶ 27); noted, but the Court did not rest its decision on the captive/open-access point.

1983849.name: Municipal Commissioner of Dum Dum Municipality v. Indian Tourism Development Corporation
1983849.proposition: Statutory corporations (including Electricity Boards under the Electricity Supply Act, 1948) are distinct juristic entities with their own funds/properties, capable of contracting and being creditors/debtors independent of the Government even where government-owned.

cited_in.title: Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. v. Raman Ispat Private Limited & Ors.
cited_in.how_treated: Applied to hold PVVNL's dues are not 'government dues' merely because of state shareholding.

Nana bin Aba v. Skeku bin Andu.name: Nana bin Aba v. Skeku bin Andu
Nana bin Aba v. Skeku bin Andu.proposition: Followed Colonial Sugar Refining on the vested, substantive nature of the right of appeal.

cited_in.title: Aruna Bhargava v. PuVVNL & Another
cited_in.how_treated: Referred within the line of authority.

1713428.name: NDMC v. Karam Chandra Thapar & Brothers Pvt. Ltd.
1713428.proposition: Liability to pay electricity charges is a statutory liability preserved by s.6 of the General Clauses Act; a bill can be issued even years after consumption.

cited_in.title: Shyam Ferrous Ltd. Gopal Nagar v. State of U.P. & 6 Others
cited_in.how_treated: Followed for the statutory-liability-preservation principle.

NESCO v. Raghunath Paper Mills (P) Ltd..name: NESCO v. Raghunath Paper Mills (P) Ltd.
NESCO v. Raghunath Paper Mills (P) Ltd..proposition: An auction purchaser buying an official liquidator's sale 'as is where is, whatever there is' is not liable for the past owner's electricity arrears, and a request for a fresh connection cannot be rejected on that ground.

cited_in.title: M/S Dharti Agro Industries Pvt. Ltd. v. The Managing Director, Pashchimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & 2 Others
cited_in.how_treated: Relied on by the petitioner as a directly analogous liquidation-sale precedent.

670840.name: New Delhi Municipal Council v. Pan Singh & Others
670840.proposition: A writ petition filed after a long time should not be entertained even if petitioners are similarly situated to those who obtained relief; delay and laches are relevant to exercise of equitable jurisdiction.

cited_in.title: M/S Three Star Paper Mills Pvt. Ltd. v. State of U.P. & 5 Ors.
cited_in.how_treated: Relied on to dismiss the claim for delay/laches.

293050.name: New Okhla Industrial Development Authority v. Kendriya Karmachari Sahkari Grih Nirman Samiti
293050.proposition: The High Court has jurisdiction under Article 226 to try issues of fact and law, but where the petition raises complex questions of fact requiring evidence, it should ordinarily decline and relegate the party to the normal remedy.

cited_in.title: Kapil Gupta v. U.P. Power Corpn. Ltd. & Anr.
cited_in.how_treated: Applied against the petitioner: complex factual disputes are better left to the appeal.

486335.name: Ningamma & Anr. v. United India Insurance Co. Ltd.
486335.proposition: A claimant is entitled to determination of just and reasonable compensation under different heads.

cited_in.title: Executive Engineer, Electricity Distribution Division-II v. State of U.P. & 2 Others
cited_in.how_treated: Applied to uphold the heads of compensation awarded.

1469962.name: Nirmala Anand v. Advent Corporation (Pvt.) Ltd.
1469962.proposition: A party cannot take advantage of its own wrong; to permit it would confer an unfair advantage.

cited_in.title: Indian Oil Corporation Ltd. v. State of U.P. & 3 Others
cited_in.how_treated: Cited (¶ 57) in support of the maxim.

1110505.name: Nizam's Institute of Medical Sciences v. Prasanth S. Dhananka & Ors.
1110505.proposition: In assessing compensation for grievous personal injury, the court strikes a balance and awards just compensation under different heads, taking guidance from Motor Vehicles Act principles.

cited_in.title: Executive Engineer, Electricity Distribution Division-II v. State of U.P. & 2 Others

1245093.name: Padmaraje R. Kadambande v. CIT
1245093.proposition: A marginal heading (e.g. 'compensation') does not control the operation or interpretation of the section.

cited_in.title: M/S Modern Rice Mill v. MVVNL & Anr.

867948.name: Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Others v. The Appellate Authority/Addl. Commissioner & Anr.
867948.citation: Civil Misc. Writ Petition No. 4222 of 2009, decided 26.3.2010
867948.proposition: The 2003 Act's scheme does not exclude a Section 126 assessment in theft cases; Section 135(1A)'s third proviso (restoration of supply on deposit of the 'assessed amount') presupposes an assessment under Section 126, covering all categories of unauthorised use including theft; the Section 127 appellate authority's power is co-extensive with the assessing authority's and extends to deciding whether the theft assessment was correctly made.

cited_in.title: M/S Trikoot Iron & Steels Castings Ltd. v. State of U.P. & Ors.

74832153.name: Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. v. DVS Steels & Alloys Pvt. Ltd.
74832153.proposition: Electricity dues are not a charge on the premises, but a distributor may stipulate, as a condition of a fresh connection, that the previous occupant's arrears be cleared; if statutory rules govern, they bind the purchaser. Provisions similar to Clause 4.3(g) and (h) of the Electricity Supply Code are necessary to safeguard the distributor.

cited_in.title: Haryana State Electricity Board v. M/s Hanuman Rice Mills, Dhanauri & Ors.
cited_in.how_treated: Relied on and quoted for the arrears/transferee synthesis.

cited_in.title: Palika Towns LLP v. State of U.P. & 2 Others
cited_in.how_treated: Surveyed and applied by analogy to hold that a specific stipulation (here, the lease deed's first-charge clause) can validly bind a purchaser to a predecessor's arrears, even outside the electricity context.

5808278.name: Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. v. Raman Ispat Private Ltd. & Ors.
5808278.proposition: In an IBC liquidation, the electricity utility is a secured creditor whose claim for arrears (secured by the Supply Code's charge) must be classified and paid per the s.53 waterfall mechanism; IBC s.238 overrides the Electricity Act/Supply Code despite their own non-obstante provisions (ss.173-174).

cited_in.title: M/S Dharti Agro Industries Pvt. Ltd. v. The Managing Director, Pashchimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & 2 Others
cited_in.how_treated: Followed as the central authority for the IBC-overrides-Electricity-Act holding.

163477337.name: Pashchimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. v. Raman Ispat Pvt. Ltd. & Ors. (NCLT Allahabad / NCLAT New Delhi)
163477337.proposition: Once a liquidation order is passed against a Corporate Debtor, the District Collector cannot separately recover/auction the Corporate Debtor's property for electricity dues under ss.173/174 of the Electricity Act, 2003, since IBC (a later Parliamentary Act) overrides; the electricity authority's remedy is to file a claim before the liquidator.

cited_in.title: Narendra Singh Panwar v. Pashchimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & 2 Others
cited_in.how_treated: Relied on by the petitioner as squarely applicable, but distinguished — that ruling concerned recovery from the Corporate Debtor's own assets/estate, not a Director's independent personal-guarantee liability.

cited_in.title: Manno Singh v. State of U.P. & Others
cited_in.how_treated: followed (as general persuasive analogue; not an electricity/Supply Code holding)

Prachi Leathers v. U.P. Power Corporatio.name: Prachi Leathers v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd.
Prachi Leathers v. U.P. Power Corporatio.proposition: Where power is taken surreptitiously/by theft (rather than under a licensee-sanctioned surcharge arrangement), a penalty rather than a mere surcharge is attracted.

cited_in.title: Northern Coalfield Ltd. v. Chairman and Managing Director, U.P. Power Corporation Ltd. & Ors.
cited_in.how_treated: Cited for the surcharge-versus-theft-penalty distinction.

395434.name: PTC India Ltd. v. CERC
395434.proposition: Regulations, as part of the regulatory framework, intervene in and even override existing contracts between regulated entities.

cited_in.title: Indian Oil Corporation Ltd. v. State of U.P. & 3 Others
cited_in.how_treated: Cited by the petitioner (¶ 28); noted, not made a basis of the decision.

cited_in.title: BSES Rajdhani Power Ltd. v. Delhi Electricity Regulatory Commission

1101587.name: Punjab State Electricity Board Ltd. v. Zora Singh & Others
1101587.proposition: The Board must supply electrical energy to consumers within a reasonable period, in order of seniority of application, per its own circulars/regulations, and must notify applicants of reasons for any delay.

cited_in.title: M/S Shri Parasnath Alloys (Pvt.) Ltd. v. Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Ors.
cited_in.how_treated: Relied on by the successful respondent to reinforce the statutory duty to supply on request.

1660026.name: R.N. Gosain v. Yashpal Dhir
1660026.proposition: Law does not permit a person to both approbate and reprobate — a party cannot accept an instrument as valid to obtain an advantage and then treat it as void to avoid a burden.

cited_in.title: Palika Towns LLP v. State of U.P. & 2 Others
cited_in.how_treated: Applied to hold the petitioner, having accepted the Transfer Memorandum/Sale Certificate, could not disclaim the arrears-payment obligation.

181377341.name: Radha Krishna Cold Storage v. State of U.P. & Others
181377341.proposition: An appeal under s.127 lies against an order that is in substance an assessment order under s.126, regardless of whether it is mislabelled as passed under s.135.

cited_in.title: Sandeep Kesarwani v. State of U.P. & 3 Others
cited_in.how_treated: Followed to confirm s.127 appellate remedy is available for theft-related assessments.

603123.name: Raghunath Rai Bareja & Anr. v. Punjab National Bank & Ors.
603123.proposition: The first and foremost rule of construction is the literal rule; where the provision is unambiguous, the court reads the statute as it is without adding words (approving Hiralal Ratanlal, Harshad S. Mehta and Patangrao Kadam).

cited_in.title: Executive Engineer, Electricity Distribution Division-II v. State of U.P. & 2 Others
cited_in.how_treated: Relied on to construe 'public utility service' literally — supply of power to the public, without importing a consumer requirement.

196522538.name: Raghvendra Garg v. State of U.P. & 5 Ors.
196522538.citation: Writ C No. 14547 of 2016, order dated 14.9.2016 (DB)
196522538.proposition: In the absence of a statutory provision, no recovery can be made from the personal assets of a company's director for the company's outstanding dues.

cited_in.title: Narendra Singh Panwar v. Pashchimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & 2 Others

180213.name: Ram Chandra Prasad Sharma & Others v. State of Bihar & Anr.
180213.proposition: In a criminal trial for theft of electrical energy under Section 39 of the Indian Electricity Act, 1910, mens rea is a relevant consideration.

515981.name: Ramakrishna Poultry (P) Ltd. v. R. Chellappan
515981.proposition: Where a landowner purchased land after a transmission-line survey/routing process was already underway, the appropriate remedy is a practical accommodation (e.g. raising line height/clearance) rather than re-routing an established transmission line, especially given the larger public interest.

743414.name: Ramchandra Dagdu Sonavane v. Vithu Hira Mahar
743414.proposition: The doctrine of res judicata (including constructive res judicata under Explanation IV, s.11 CPC) applies broadly, barring re-litigation of matters that were or ought to have been raised in an earlier proceeding.

cited_in.title: Orissa Power Transmission Corporation Ltd. & Ors. v. Asian School of Business Management Trust & Ors.
cited_in.how_treated: Applied to hold that the second writ petition, seeking substantially the same relief as the first (dismissed) petition, was barred.

1757511.name: Ramesh Singh v. Cinta Devi
1757511.proposition: A vested right of appeal under the old Motor Vehicles Act is not dislodged by the new Act; the appellant may appeal without the pre-deposit required by the proviso to s.173 of the new Act.

cited_in.title: Aruna Bhargava v. PuVVNL & Another
cited_in.how_treated: Followed as the most apt authority.

123741567.name: Rana Girders Ltd. (excise dues case)
123741567.proposition: A purchaser's statutory-liability undertaking limited to liabilities 'arising out of the land/building/machinery' does not extend to excise dues, which arise from manufacturing activity, not the property itself.

cited_in.title: Palika Towns LLP v. State of U.P. & 2 Others
cited_in.how_treated: Distinguished — held inapplicable since lease rent (unlike excise duty) does arise directly from the leasehold property itself.

193909.name: Ravi Shanker Giri v. Sub-Divisional Officer, U.P. Power Corporation Ltd. & Others

1865062.name: Raymond Ltd. & Anr. v. M.P. Electricity Board & Ors.

577956.name: Raymond Ltd. v. State of Chhattisgarh & Ors.

559116.name: Sri Bhagwan Gupta v. Kanpur Electricity Supply Company Ltd. & Ors.

cited_in.title: Lalit Kumar Kapoor v. Kanpur Electricity Supply Company & Anr.
cited_in.how_treated: Given only persuasive value; not followed — the Court held that the law as of the date of the FINAL assessment (not the date the cause of action arose) governs the applicable rate.

cited_in.title: M/S Venus Stone Crushing Co. & Anr. v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd. & Ors.
cited_in.how_treated: Followed (via Modern Rice Mill).

163084985.name: State Bank of India v. V. Ramakrishnan & Anr.
163084985.proposition: The s.14 IBC moratorium applies only to the Corporate Debtor and its own assets/proceedings, not to a personal guarantor of the Corporate Debtor; a plain reading of s.14 conspicuously omits any mention of the personal guarantor.

cited_in.title: Narendra Singh Panwar v. Pashchimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & 2 Others
cited_in.how_treated: Applied as the governing precedent to hold that the s.14 moratorium does not shield the Director-guarantor from recovery.

State Load Despatch Centre v. GERC.name: State Load Despatch Centre v. GERC
State Load Despatch Centre v. GERC.proposition: 'Truing up' means the adjustment of actual amounts incurred against the estimated/projected amounts determined under the ARR.

cited_in.title: BSES Rajdhani Power Ltd. v. Delhi Electricity Regulatory Commission
cited_in.how_treated: Referred to define truing up.

970048.name: State of A.P. v. National Thermal Power Corporation Ltd.
970048.proposition: Electricity is 'goods'; a purchaser is liable to pay for it, the quantum and time of payment being ascertained post facto by agreement or statute.

cited_in.title: Assistant Engineer (D1), Ajmer Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Anr. v. Rahamatullah Khan alias Rahamjulla
cited_in.how_treated: Referred to characterise the nature of electricity charges.

910514.name: State of Bihar & Others v. Subhash Singh
910514.proposition: State action must be carried out in accordance with the Constitution and within legal limits; judicial review can examine constitutionality and procedural legality of administrative action.

cited_in.title: M/S Om Ice Factory Thru' Its Partner Satyapal Singh v. Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Anr.
cited_in.how_treated: Held inapplicable — the assessing authority's decision was not shown to be dehors the law or established procedure.

1287305.name: State of Bihar v. P.P. Sharma
1287305.proposition: A person against whom mala fides or bias is imputed must be impleaded eo nomine and given an opportunity to meet the allegation; absent this, no enquiry into mala fides can be made.

cited_in.title: M/S Beeco Electrical India & Anr. v. Pashchimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Ors.
cited_in.how_treated: Relied on for dismissing the petitioner's unimpleaded mala fide plea.

State of Bombay v. Supreme General Films.name: State of Bombay v. Supreme General Films Exchange Ltd.
State of Bombay v. Supreme General Films.proposition: To the same effect on the vested right of appeal.

cited_in.title: Aruna Bhargava v. PuVVNL & Another
cited_in.how_treated: Referred (within Ramesh Singh).

1033637.name: State of Haryana v. Bhajan Lal
1033637.proposition: Courts should not interfere with investigation or quash an FIR unless no cognizable offence is ex-facie discernible from the allegations, or a statutory restriction bars the police from investigating.

cited_in.title: Pawan Kumar Laur v. State of U.P. & Others
cited_in.how_treated: Applied (via Ajit Singh @ Muraha and Satya Pal) as the governing standard to decline quashing the FIR.

900221.name: State of Maharashtra v. Laljit Rajashi Shah & Ors.
900221.proposition: A person deemed a public servant under an analogous 'deemed to be public servant' provision for Maharashtra Cooperative Societies employees was not a public servant for purposes of the (former) Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947.

cited_in.title: Naresh Kumar Madan v. State of Madhya Pradesh
cited_in.how_treated: Distinguished — that case concerned a cooperative-society member, not an employee of a statutory corporation, and did not address the 1988 Act's broader definition.

399238.name: State of Orissa v. Bimal Kumar Mohanty
399238.proposition: Suspension should not be passed as an administrative routine or mechanically; it requires consideration of the gravity of alleged misconduct and the evidence, applying the disciplinary authority's mind.

cited_in.title: Shabih Haider v. State of U.P. thru. Prin. Secy., Housing & Urban Planning & Ors.
cited_in.how_treated: Applied as the governing standard to quash the suspension order.

847902.name: State of Orissa v. Pyari Mohan Samantaray & Others
847902.proposition: Reiterates that unexplained delay disentitles a petitioner to discretionary relief under Article 226.

cited_in.title: M/S Three Star Paper Mills Pvt. Ltd. v. State of U.P. & 5 Ors.
cited_in.how_treated: Relied on.

State of U.P. v. Aditya Prasad Srivastav.name: State of U.P. v. Aditya Prasad Srivastava
State of U.P. v. Aditya Prasad Srivastav.proposition: Same principle on proof of charges in a departmental inquiry.

cited_in.title: Dhirendra Kumar Chaudhary v. State of U.P. & 5 Others
cited_in.how_treated: Referred within the catena.

1276201.name: State of U.P. v. Brij Bhushan Sharma
1276201.citation: Writ Petition No. 474 (SB) of 2011 (Allahabad HC, DB)
1276201.proposition: The practice of the State filing frivolous writ petitions challenging tribunal orders is deprecated.

cited_in.title: Kanpur Electricity Supply Co. Ltd. & Anr. v. U.P. Electricity Regulatory Commission & Ors.
cited_in.how_treated: Referred to the same effect in imposing costs.

State of U.P. v. Kishori Lal.name: State of U.P. v. Kishori Lal
State of U.P. v. Kishori Lal.proposition: Same principle on the Establishment's burden to prove charges in a departmental inquiry.

cited_in.title: Dhirendra Kumar Chaudhary v. State of U.P. & 5 Others
cited_in.how_treated: Referred within the catena.

1064026.name: State of U.P. v. Saroj Kumar Sinha
1064026.proposition: In a departmental inquiry the Establishment must prove the charges by leading evidence; an inquiry officer is not to act as a prosecutor, and charges are not self-proving.

cited_in.title: Dhirendra Kumar Chaudhary v. State of U.P. & 5 Others
cited_in.how_treated: Relied on for the burden-of-proof principle in major-penalty inquiries.

157762969.name: State of U.P. v. Suresh Kumar
157762969.citation: Writ Petition No. 506 (S/B) of 2011 (Allahabad HC, DB)
157762969.proposition: The State and its instrumentalities should refrain from filing frivolous petitions that waste the Court's time.

cited_in.title: Kanpur Electricity Supply Co. Ltd. & Anr. v. U.P. Electricity Regulatory Commission & Ors.
cited_in.how_treated: Referred to deprecate the licensee's frivolous writ petition.

1693089.name: State of Uttaranchal v. Kharak Singh
1693089.proposition: Natural justice in disciplinary inquiries requires evidence to be led and the delinquent given opportunity to meet it.

cited_in.title: Dhirendra Kumar Chaudhary v. State of U.P. & 5 Others
cited_in.how_treated: Relied on within the natural-justice line.

186684406.name: State Tax Officer v. Rainbow Papers Ltd.
186684406.proposition: A statutory first-charge provision (s.48, Gujarat VAT Act) makes the State a 'secured creditor' under the IBC, since the definition of 'secured creditor' does not exclude government/statutory charges; a resolution plan excluding such dues is not IBC-compliant and not binding on the State.

cited_in.title: Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. v. Raman Ispat Private Limited & Ors.
cited_in.how_treated: Distinguished and confined to its facts — did not consider or apply the s.53 waterfall mechanism, arose in a resolution-plan (not liquidation) context, and cannot be extended to give government/quasi-government dues priority over the deliberately structured s.53 hierarchy.

Sundaresh Bhatt, Liquidator of ABG Shipy.name: Sundaresh Bhatt, Liquidator of ABG Shipyard v. Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs
Sundaresh Bhatt, Liquidator of ABG Shipy.proposition: IBC prevails over the Customs Act, 1962 once moratorium is imposed; the customs authority retains only a limited jurisdiction to assess duty, not to recover by sale/confiscation.

cited_in.title: M/S Dharti Agro Industries Pvt. Ltd. v. The Managing Director, Pashchimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & 2 Others
cited_in.how_treated: Relied on (via Raman Ispat) as an analogous application of s.238 primacy over a sectoral statute with its own first-charge provision.

cited_in.title: Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. v. Raman Ispat Private Limited & Ors.
cited_in.how_treated: Applied by analogy to hold IBC s.238 similarly overrides the Electricity Act's ss.173/174 independent-recovery mechanism.

Swastic Industries v. Maharashtra State.name: Swastic Industries v. Maharashtra State Electricity Board

cited_in.title: Assistant Engineer (D1), Ajmer Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Anr. v. Rahamatullah Khan alias Rahamjulla
cited_in.how_treated: Relied on to separate the right to recover from the remedy of disconnection.

Tanveer Azam v. State of U.P. & Others (.name: Tanveer Azam v. State of U.P. & Others (also cited as Iftikhar Ahsan v. State of U.P.)
Tanveer Azam v. State of U.P. & Others (.citation: Writ Petition No. 71425 of 2013, order dated 3.1.2014
Tanveer Azam v. State of U.P. & Others (.proposition: Same as Ravi Shankar Giri — owner's consent required under the Code for grant of electricity connection.

cited_in.title: Seema Mansoor v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd. & 3 Others
cited_in.how_treated: Overruled/held not to lay down correct law, for the same reasons as Ravi Shankar Giri.

Tata Power Co. Ltd. v. Reliance Energy L.name: Tata Power Co. Ltd. v. Reliance Energy Ltd.

cited_in.title: Assistant Engineer (D1), Ajmer Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Anr. v. Rahamatullah Khan alias Rahamjulla
cited_in.how_treated: Referred for the statute's consumer-protective character.

183986005.name: Tata Power Western Odisha Distribution Ltd. v. Jagannath Sponge Private Ltd.
183986005.proposition: Following Raman Ispat, a power distribution company cannot insist on payment of the corporate debtor's arrears (to be paid per the IBC waterfall mechanism) as a precondition for granting an electricity connection to the successful resolution applicant.

cited_in.title: M/S Dharti Agro Industries Pvt. Ltd. v. The Managing Director, Pashchimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & 2 Others
cited_in.how_treated: Relied on by the petitioner as a further application of Raman Ispat.

60837656.name: Telangana State Southern Power Distribution Company Ltd. v. ...
60837656.proposition: Electricity dues, where statutory in character under the Electricity Act and the terms/conditions of supply, cannot be waived (s.56, Electricity Act 2003 / pari materia s.24, 1910 Act); where an e-auction notice specifically flags existing electricity dues as a purchaser liability on an 'AS IS WHERE IS, WITHOUT RECOURSE' basis, the purchaser is liable to pay them.

cited_in.title: Palika Towns LLP v. State of U.P. & 2 Others
cited_in.how_treated: Applied by analogy — held to support (not assist) GNIDA's position, since the lease deed/Transfer Memorandum here similarly and specifically flagged the arrears as a purchaser liability.

1202878.name: The Management of Hotel Imperial, New Delhi v. Hotel Workers' Union
1202878.proposition: The power to suspend is a creature of statute or contract, to be exercised keeping in view the letter and spirit of the statute.

cited_in.title: Shabih Haider v. State of U.P. thru. Prin. Secy., Housing & Urban Planning & Ors.
cited_in.how_treated: Cited (via Dhirendra Kumar Rai) for the statutory basis of suspension power.

693740.name: The State of Orissa v. Madan Gopal Rungta
693740.proposition: Article 226 cannot be used to grant interim relief as the only and final relief; interim relief is available only as ancillary to a final relief obtainable in a proceeding actually pending and to be decided on merits before that court.

cited_in.title: Om Prakash s/o Gauri Shankar v. Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Ors.
cited_in.how_treated: Applied as the controlling authority to reject the petitioner's request for interim protection after withdrawing the writ petition.

864296.name: Tinsukhia Electricity Supply Co. Ltd. v. State of Assam & Ors.
864296.proposition: A statute must be construed so as to make it effective and operative ('ut res magis valeat quam pereat'); courts should avoid interpretations reducing a provision to futility.

cited_in.title: Sandeep Kesarwani v. State of U.P. & 3 Others
cited_in.how_treated: Applied to support a harmonious, purposive reading of ss.126 and 135 that gives effect to both provisions rather than rendering s.126 inoperative in theft cases.

Tirumala Modern Rice Mill v. Transmissio.name: Tirumala Modern Rice Mill v. Transmission Corporation of A.P. Ltd. (AP Transco)

cited_in.title: Sandeep Kesarwani v. State of U.P. & 3 Others
cited_in.how_treated: Held not to lay down the proposition that s.126 assessment is inapplicable to theft cases; distinguished as not supporting the petitioner's submission.

Transmission Corpn. of A.P. Ltd. v. Sri.name: Transmission Corpn. of A.P. Ltd. v. Sri Rama Krishna Rice Mill
Transmission Corpn. of A.P. Ltd. v. Sri.proposition: In an electricity assessment dispute, merely taking note of the objections filed is not compliance with the relevant rules; natural justice is not a straitjacket formula and varies with the circumstances.

cited_in.title: Hazi Mohd. Yaseen v. P.V.V.N.L. & Another
cited_in.how_treated: Relied on / discussed for the content of the opportunity of hearing in the consumer-electricity context.

107041.name: Transmission Corporation of A.P. Ltd. & Ors. v. Sri Rama Krishna Rice Mill
107041.proposition: Explains the standard of reasonable opportunity of hearing in the context of an electricity assessment.

cited_in.title: Lalit Kumar Kapoor v. Kanpur Electricity Supply Company & Anr.
cited_in.how_treated: Relied on to the same effect as Khem Chand.

cited_in.title: M/S Beeco Electrical India & Anr. v. Pashchimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Ors.
cited_in.how_treated: Held inapplicable — the petitioner failed to show inadequate opportunity, and his objections were in fact considered and discussed in the assessment order.

U.P. Power Corporation Ltd. v. M/s Lohia.name: U.P. Power Corporation Ltd. v. M/s Lohia Brass Pvt. Ltd. & Others
U.P. Power Corporation Ltd. v. M/s Lohia.proposition: Peak-hour-restriction violation penalty is to be imposed per inspection report (first violation and subsequently for every violation), settling the correct computation formula.

cited_in.title: Shyam Ferrous Ltd. Gopal Nagar v. State of U.P. & 6 Others

1267330.name: U.P. Rajkiya Nirman Nigam Ltd. v. Indure Pvt. Ltd.
1267330.proposition: (Same principle as Karnal Improvement Trust — acquiescence does not confer jurisdiction.)

cited_in.title: M.D., Pakshimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. v. Electricity Ombudsman & Anr.
cited_in.how_treated: Relied on to the same effect.

1915317.name: Uma Nath Pandey & Ors. v. State of U.P. & Anr.
1915317.proposition: Natural justice is another name for common-sense justice; adherence to its principles is of supreme importance whenever a quasi-judicial body or an administrative action involving civil consequences is in issue.

cited_in.title: Navi Hasan v. U.P. Power Corporation & Another
cited_in.how_treated: Applied as the governing authority on the audi alteram partem principle to quash the impugned demand order.

Union of India v. Jyoti Prakash Mitter.name: Union of India v. Jyoti Prakash Mitter

cited_in.title: Hazi Mohd. Yaseen v. P.V.V.N.L. & Another

767596.name: Union of India v. Prakash P. Hinduja & Another
767596.proposition: Section 482 Cr.P.C. power to quash criminal proceedings may be exercised (sparingly, with circumspection) where the FIR/complaint even taken at face value discloses no offence, or the uncontroverted allegations/evidence do not disclose commission of any offence, or there is an express legal bar to continuance of proceedings.

cited_in.title: Saurabh Agrawal & Another v. State of U.P. & Others
cited_in.how_treated: Applied as the governing standard for quashing the s.135 prosecution.

1961694.name: Union of India v. Rallia Ram
1961694.proposition: Interest is payable in equity only where circumstances attract equitable jurisdiction, or under the Interest Act, or where an agreement/statute/trade usage so provides.

cited_in.title: M/S NTPC Ltd. v. M.P. State Electricity Board & Ors. (with connected appeals)
cited_in.how_treated: Relied on to reject the equity-based interest claim absent any such basis.

823952.name: Union of India v. Watkins Mayor and Co.
823952.proposition: Interest is claimable only where there is an agreement, trade usage having force of law, or a substantive statutory provision; equity alone cannot justify an interest claim.

cited_in.title: M/S NTPC Ltd. v. M.P. State Electricity Board & Ors. (with connected appeals)
cited_in.how_treated: Relied on to the same effect.

622189.name: United Commercial Bank Ltd. v. Their Workmen
622189.proposition: No acquiescence or consent can give a jurisdiction to a court of limited jurisdiction which it does not possess.

cited_in.title: M.D., Pakshimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. v. Electricity Ombudsman & Anr.
cited_in.how_treated: Relied on for the no-jurisdiction-by-consent principle.

1100992.name: United India Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Ajay Sinha
1100992.proposition: A Permanent Lok Adalat does not act merely as an arbitrator whose award may be challenged; Parliament has given it an adjudicatory role to decide the matter.

cited_in.title: Executive Engineer, Electricity Distribution Division-II v. State of U.P. & 2 Others

726134.name: United India Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Lehru & Ors.
726134.proposition: (Cited alongside Saurashtra Chemicals in support of the petitioners' 'subject to' argument.)

cited_in.how_treated: Referred.

Vitthalbhai Narangbhai Patel v. CST.name: Vitthalbhai Narangbhai Patel v. CST

1125536.name: Yunus v. State of Maharashtra & Others
